courses.title: Claude Foundations
courses.tagline: What Claude is and what it can do
courses.description: Start here. Learn what Claude is, the model family, and the core ideas behind safe, helpful AI.

questions.question: What is Claude?
options: An AI assistant made by Anthropic
questions.explanation: Claude is a family of AI assistants created by Anthropic, designed to be helpful, honest, and harmless.

questions.question: Which company builds Claude?
questions.explanation: Anthropic is an AI safety company and the maker of the Claude model family.

questions.question: Claude is designed around three core values. Which set is correct?
questions.explanation: Anthropic designs Claude to be helpful, honest, and harmless — often called the three H's.

questions.question: Which of these can Claude help you do?
questions.explanation: Claude is a general-purpose assistant: writing, analysis, coding, summarising, brainstorming and more.

questions.question: How do you interact with Claude in a chat?
options: By writing prompts in natural language
questions.explanation: You talk to Claude in plain language. Clear, specific prompts get the best results.

questions.question: Which Claude model tier is optimised for speed and efficiency?
questions.explanation: Haiku is the fastest, most lightweight tier — great for quick, high-volume tasks.

questions.question: For deep reasoning on the hardest problems, which classic tier would you pick?
questions.explanation: Opus is the high-capability tier for complex, multi-step reasoning tasks.

questions.question: What is a 'context window'?
options: How much text the model can consider at once
The time a session stays open
questions.explanation: The context window is the amount of conversation and documents the model can hold in mind at one time.

questions.question: A 'token' is best described as…
options: A small chunk of text the model reads or writes
questions.explanation: Models process text as tokens — pieces of words. Costs and limits are usually measured in tokens.

questions.question: Claude can work with images in a conversation. This ability is called…
questions.explanation: Vision lets Claude read screenshots, photos, charts and diagrams you attach.

questions.question: What is an AI 'hallucination'?
options: A confident answer that is actually wrong or made up
questions.explanation: Models can state incorrect things confidently. Always verify important facts from primary sources.

questions.question: What is the safest habit when Claude gives you a critical fact or figure?
options: Verify it against a trusted source
questions.explanation: Treat model output as a strong draft, not ground truth — verify anything high-stakes.

questions.question: 'Constitutional AI' refers to…
options: Training AI using a written set of principles
questions.explanation: Anthropic trains Claude with a 'constitution' — explicit principles that guide safe, helpful behaviour.

questions.question: Which of these should you avoid pasting into any AI chat at work?
options: A draft of a public blog post
questions.explanation: Follow your organisation's data policy — keep confidential and personal data out of tools that aren't approved for it.

questions.question: If Claude refuses a request, the best next step is to…
options: Rephrase honestly and explain your legitimate goal
questions.explanation: Explaining your real intent and context usually helps Claude assist safely and accurately.

courses.title: Prompting Mastery
courses.description: Learn the craft of writing prompts: clarity, context, examples, structure, and iteration.

questions.question: Which prompt will get the best result?
options: "Write a 100-word friendly intro about beagles for a pet-shop newsletter"
questions.explanation: Specific prompts — audience, length, tone, topic — consistently beat vague ones.

questions.question: What is the 'golden rule' of prompting?
options: Keep every prompt under ten words
If a colleague would be confused by your request, the model will be too
questions.explanation: Show your prompt to a colleague: if they can't follow it, neither can the model. Write for a smart newcomer.

questions.question: Why does giving context improve answers?
options: The model tailors its answer to your situation and goal
questions.explanation: Purpose, audience, and constraints let the model choose the right content, tone and depth.

questions.question: You want the answer as a table. What should you do?
options: Say so explicitly: "Present the result as a table with columns X and Y"
questions.explanation: State the output format you want — lists, tables, JSON, word counts. The model follows explicit format requests.

questions.question: Your first answer isn't quite right. The best move is to…
options: Tell the model what to change and iterate
questions.explanation: Prompting is iterative: give feedback ('shorter', 'more formal', 'add examples') and refine.

questions.question: Showing the model 2–3 examples of the output you want is called…
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting — including worked examples — is one of the most reliable ways to shape output.

questions.question: "You are an experienced HR manager reviewing this policy…" is an example of…
questions.explanation: Assigning a role focuses the model's expertise, tone and point of view.

questions.question: Asking the model to 'think step by step' before answering helps because…
options: Working through reasoning first improves accuracy on complex problems
questions.explanation: Chain-of-thought prompting gives the model room to reason before committing to an answer.

questions.question: When pasting a long document to analyse, a good practice is to…
options: Put your instructions after/around clearly separated document text
Mix instructions randomly inside the document
questions.explanation: Separate data from instructions (e.g. with headings or XML-style tags) so the model knows what is content vs. command.

questions.question: Which request best 'prefills' the answer style you want?
options: "Answer as bullet points starting each with a verb"
questions.explanation: Prescribing the opening style or skeleton of the answer strongly steers the result.

questions.question: You need to summarise a 40-page report for executives. The best prompt includes…
options: Audience, length, focus areas, and the format you need
Just the report with no instructions
A request to rewrite the whole report
questions.explanation: "Summarise for the exec team in 5 bullet points focused on cost and risk" beats a bare 'summarise'.

questions.question: For brainstorming, which technique yields the most useful ideas?
options: Ask for many varied ideas with constraints, then iterate on the best
Ask for ideas without any topic
Ask the model to decide everything
questions.explanation: Quantity plus constraints ('10 ideas, each under 15 words, for a B2B audience') then refine the winners.

questions.question: You're drafting an email in a delicate situation. What extra context helps most?
options: Your relationship to the reader and the outcome you want
questions.explanation: Relationship, history, tone and desired outcome let the model hit the right register.

questions.question: The model's draft contains a factual claim you'll publish. You should…
options: Ask the model to cite sources and verify them yourself
Assume it's correct because it sounds confident
questions.explanation: For public content, check claims against reliable sources — the author is still you.

questions.question: Which is a good 'meta' habit to improve your prompting over time?
options: Keep a library of prompts that worked well for you
Always write prompts from scratch at random
questions.explanation: Saving and refining your best prompts builds a personal toolkit that compounds.

courses.title: Claude at Work
courses.description: Use Claude's power features: projects, artifacts, file analysis, connectors and coding help.

questions.question: Claude can read files you attach. Which of these is a typical use?
options: Extracting a table from a spreadsheet
Answering questions about a slide deck
questions.explanation: Attach PDFs, spreadsheets, docs and images and ask questions, request summaries or transformations.

questions.question: What is an 'Artifact' in the Claude app?
options: A separate live document/preview Claude creates alongside chat (code, docs, designs)
questions.explanation: Artifacts are standalone outputs — documents, code, diagrams, mini-apps — shown next to the conversation.

questions.question: 'Projects' in Claude are useful because they…
options: Hold shared context, files and instructions for ongoing work
Make Claude respond in emoji only
questions.explanation: A project keeps documents and custom instructions attached so every chat starts informed.

questions.question: When asking Claude to analyse data, the best first step is to…
options: Describe what the data is and what decision you're trying to make
questions.explanation: Framing the decision ('which region should we invest in?') turns generic stats into useful analysis.

questions.question: Claude for coding can…
questions.explanation: From explaining to writing to debugging — describe the goal and share the relevant code or error.

questions.question: Which task is Claude LEAST suited for without human review?
options: Final legal advice for a contract dispute
questions.explanation: High-stakes legal, medical or financial decisions need qualified human professionals; Claude can assist, not decide.

questions.question: A teammate asks how you made a great AI-assisted report. Good practice is to…
options: Share the prompt and approach you used
questions.explanation: Sharing prompts and workflows lifts the whole team — treat them like reusable templates.

questions.question: The most reliable way to get better at using Claude is…
options: Regular practice on real tasks with iteration
questions.explanation: Skill comes from reps: use it on real work, notice what helps, refine your prompts.

questions.question: Before automating a workflow with AI, you should first…
options: Do it manually with the AI a few times to learn the failure modes
questions.explanation: Manual runs reveal where the model shines and where it stumbles — then automate with the right checks.

questions.question: Which statement about AI at work is most accurate?
options: AI is a powerful collaborator; you stay accountable for the result
AI should never be used at work
AI removes the need to understand your field
questions.explanation: Think of Claude as a brilliant, fast collaborator whose work you review and own.
